- Thresholds become the acceptance bar referenced by e3.1

nodes.title: Spike: episode segmentation accuracy on real agent-driven histories
nodes.description: Segmentation is the load-bearing assumption of the whole product. Collect 200 agent turns from real sessions, hand-annotate the true episode boundaries, then compare boundary precision and recall for three strategies: time/author heuristics only, hook-event-driven boundaries, and trailers plus message-shape signals. Also measure how often segmentation mistakes would hide a real problem (i.e. a pathology spans a wrong boundary).
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Annotated ground truth for 200 turns committed to the fixture corpus
- Precision and recall table for the three strategies
- Recommended default rule set with the failure modes enumerated
- Recommendation folded into ADR-003 before e1.3 is built

nodes.title: Spike: cost of full graph-per-revision at 10k commits
nodes.description: Epic 3 assumes a graph snapshot per revision is affordable with structural sharing; measure it before e3.2 is designed. Prototype snapshot storage with and without sharing, measure time and bytes per commit on a real 10k-commit repository, measure incremental query latency, and test alternative invalidation policies (full snapshot every N commits plus a delta window, on-demand recomputation, content-defined chunking). DONE: five strategies written into ADR-004 §4.6's real DDL and run over a 10 004-commit repository (2 298 modules, 54 025 graph rows); decision in ADR-004 §14.1, tables generated from benchmarks/reports/s3-graph-snapshots.json, method and limits in docs/concepts/graph-storage.md.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Measured time and bytes per revision for each strategy
- Recommended invalidation and storage policy with the numbers behind it
- Latency figures for the queries the TUI actually issues
- Decision recorded in ADR-004 and reflected in e3.2's approach

nodes.title: Spike: rename and copy detection reliability across merges
nodes.description: Folder-structure stories fall over if rename detection is wrong. Compare git rename detection, a content-similarity matcher and a hybrid on fixtures including rename-with-rewrite, file split and merge, renames that cross a merge commit and renames introduced by a rebase. Report how often a wrong pairing would mislead a reviewer, which is more damaging than a missing pairing.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Precision and recall per algorithm across the rename fixture set
- Thresholds and confidence calibration documented
- Recommendation for what to show as fact vs as a guess
- Findings reflected in e2.4's approach

nodes.title: Spike: does LLM narrative polish beat the deterministic template
nodes.description: Decide whether e4.7's optional LLM path earns its complexity. Generate episode narratives both ways for 20 real episodes, have three reviewers rate accuracy, usefulness and trustworthiness blind, and specifically count hallucinated claims not supported by the evidence set. Also record cost, latency and determinism.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Blind comparison ratings from three reviewers with hallucination counts per approach
- Cost and latency table per episode
- Written recommendation: ship the opt-in path, ship nothing, or gate it behind further work
- Outcome recorded as a decision issue linked from e4.7

nodes.title: Milestone: Alpha - spine usable for daily review
nodes.description: Alpha gate: epics 0 and 1 are complete and the tool is genuinely useful for reviewing an agent-generated repository day to day, even with no analysis at all. Publish alpha binaries, announce to a small group and start collecting real usage.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- All Epic 0 and Epic 1 tickets closed with no open P1 defects
- Spike recommendations reflected in the plan (e0.12 done)
- Alpha artifacts installable on three OSes
- At least three people outside the core team using it weekly

nodes.title: Milestone: Beta - change intelligence, attention queue and export
nodes.description: Beta gate: a reviewer can work the attention queue, understand dependencies, structure and non-code surfaces, and export a sign-off artefact that lands on a PR, with harness intent flowing in. Open the beta loop and start dogfooding Fathom on Fathom.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Epic 2 complete; the core tickets of epics 4, 5 and 6 listed as dependencies are closed
- Risk-score false-positive rate under the threshold agreed in e0.12 on three real repos
- Export artefact used in at least one real PR review outside this project
- No open P1 defects against the beta scope

nodes.title: Milestone: 1.0 - architecture awareness, CI gate and packaging
nodes.description: 1.0 gate: architecture deltas, cycles, layering and API surface are visible and enforceable, the agent can query the same model over MCP, CI can block on new violations, packaging and docs are credible, and the hardening sweep has been run. This is the release where Fathom plus a coding harness is a defensible answer to 'how do I deliver agentic software with confidence'.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- All epic 3 and epic 6 tickets closed; epic 7 hardening items closed or consciously deferred with a written reason
- fathom check running in at least two external CI pipelines
- Docs, demo repository and five-minute demo published
- Perf budgets met or consciously restated in ADR-004
